content: I would like to add that for a game that has a horizontal build focus, I agree with having the additional modifiers. Whether it be restrictions or buffs or strange new mechanics, getting an edge at nightmare and madness bosses beyond just "have OE or AA" would make it more engaging.

**D-Zone**: i frequently feel like one difficulty is too easy, but the next one is too hard, so i think we need more difficulty tiers in-between.
on top of that, the extra clear teams that would normally be the most appropriate choice could be underinvested, a choice to lower difficulty for it while still rewarding it would smooth out the progression.

higher difficulty tiers would be good as long as there's no pressure for extra rewards,
but i think it would be a better idea to add it as a reward for disabling OE/AA instead,
this would both raise the difficulty and make it easier to keep the promise of not balancing the endgame around E3.

D-Zone **revives**: i think the biggest problem with them is the impact on replays/records, i use them to learn more about the game, and revives would either promote bad playstyles if they're not hidden, or promote high spenders if they are. both options are bad for learning.

Covenant **Bonding**: it would be a good change if substats didn't exist in the first place,
i'm already burnt out from rolling substats from other games, but i think it can still be salvaged by creating a new resource/mechanic that makes it significantly easier to get perfect substats.
-# e.g. choose 1-2 of substats to reroll as perfect chosen substats, but make it impossible to revert the bond other than complete dissolution. this would also make a better reward for the higher D-Zone difficulty tiers.

**Traphase**: i think the biggest problem is that it's completely different from main game, so there's too much to learn, but not enough incentive to do so. a PvE mode with better rewards and preset/reduced choice of characters would've been an easy fix.

**Affinity/Attunement**: it's still too expensive, why not just remove it from shops entirely and turn it into a high-tier reward for D-Zone or events?
And i'd rather see it as a way to show mastery rather than investment, so why not just reward affinity past 15 only when used in D-Zone clears?

I’m okay with D-Tides being more difficult.
 However, I don’t agree with the way the game’s difficulty is increasing compared to the growth of our units. As mentioned in this thread, to make a unit stronger, you either need to get copies of that specific character or increase their level.
 With the current D-Tide system, it’s only possible to raise 5 characters to level 80 per year. That’s not enough when you look at the level requirements displayed for the new D-Tide stages.
 With the D-Tide update, it will be possible to raise 10 characters to level 80 per year, which seems much more reasonable to me. 

However, the fact that these additional resources are locked behind the hardmode D-Tides makes no sense. I should be able to upgrade my characters in order to tackle this difficult content, not because I’ve already managed to clear it.
 How is a new player supposed to access the hardest difficulty it it take a year to get a team to 80 ? You’d need 4 years to get the 5 team to max level.

Posting here what I did on Reddit: Putting aside the issue of emergency gnosis, I wanted to propose a different solution to giving whales a way to compete for the dtide leaderboards rather than nightmare and madness mode. To me, massive hp inflation is more tedious than fun, and madness mode having 9x the hp of current alert 5 sounds very unfun. It will lead to more cheesy strats and less diverse gameplay. Just look at madness rail, which is almost all Clem teams, and madness pdive, which is almost all Gmurphy and Tawil teams.

In current dtide, there is an amazing variety of teams and strategies. Sure, there are common cores of teams that appear often, but it really is awesome to look at the leaderboards and see many differences between teams, wheels, and tactics. To some extent, this reflects the fact that you need multiple teams. But it also reflects the creativity that is possible at the current level of balance.

Instead of making hp sponges in nightmare and madness dtide, which will severely limit the leaderboard meta, I think a more simple, elegant solution would be to allow another extra clear. This would not affect the people who just want to do a single clear to rush for their biweekly dtide rewards. But it would allow whales to use the many characters they’ve built up over the years in new and interesting teams to strive for a 450 score, and keep an incentive for whales to pull for older characters, too. Personally, as a whale who gets 425 every dtide (and then has little to do afterwards), I would much rather try to clear another set of teams in alert 5 with wonky underused awakeners than have hp-inflated enemies that require specific, preset strategies. To me, that leans away from the strength of Morimens’s gameplay rather than towards it.

I would also add that I don’t mind some hp inflation. That’s inevitable in gacha games, and there has been reasonable hp inflation over time in dtide so far. But a jump to 9x hp seems extreme and less fun to me

But removing the reward just because newer players can't reach it right now would defeat the purpose of having an endgame difficulty in the first place. If every reward has to be immediately accessible to new players, there will eventually be nothing meaningful left for veteran players to chase. In comparison, for a new player who can't get to higher difficult yet, before the update, they get nothing; after the update, they can get something after a while. For a player that don't want to try, before and after the update they get nothing, it's the same. my 2nd feedback this time

For dtide 
1) The new system favours vertically invested teams instead of horizontal invested teams. Since points increase by 10 each difficulty, while doing an extra clear on the same difficulty gives only 5 points. 

What does this mean? This causes less team building variety and encourages pulling for absolute axiom AA to make a single team clear the highest difficulty for the most points. 

Who does this affect? Mostly free to play / low spender players that have a wide roster of low invested e0~e3 units. This is basically the majority of the player base. 

My thoughts is to rework the point system that balances both vertical & horizontal investment. Much like the current dtide 10x alert 4 = 5x alert 5 = 400 points

2)The new nightmare / madness difficulties seemingly only have their hp increase 2-3x and damage 30-60% each tier. 

What does this mean? This either translate to 1 or 2 things. Either, existing units have to be buffed in order to make them viable against this difficulty and future releasing units will have increasing higher power floor / ceilings. If that is not the case, this means pulling for OE/AA becomes an ever increasing demand just to play higher level difficulties in dtide. 

Who does this affect? Majority of the player base who are not whales / big spenders. 

My thoughts are if BIAV cares about powercreep and truly believes in what they said about “OE/AA being not needed in content”, explore different ways to increase dtide difficulty instead of blinding increasing hp & damage. 

Allowing skill expression is satisfying thing in morimens and should be prioritise instead of wallet flexing. 

I hope biav looks into this seriously as this is likely the biggest factor that can improve or worsen the game’s power creep, monetisation, and balance.

I think covenant bonding is a great and cheap way to empower a set of covenant, and would benefit new and old players alike. It would be a good change as long as new content are not heavily balanced around bonded covenants.

content:
Some basic features to make rearranging teams and managing WoDs for each character easier. Currently, whenever we move a character from one team to another, they don't retain the WoD settings defined for the previous team. Often, a character works well with the same WoDs across all teams, and we want them to keep those same settings regardless of which team they are moved to. Ideally:
- WoDs would be set on the character information screen.
- It would be possible to change a character's position in the team simply by dragging them.
seems like concerns from neither side got addressed
我的建議是：恢復新角色的pvp 更新

Part 1
=====
Emergency Gnosis
Keeping it to cost only 1 is better to avoid confusion and inconsistencies with the other modes since it doesn't count towards the ranking anyway, but if it has to cost 3 for whatever reason, I'm personally fine with it.

Bonding Covenant
I'm not against it, and since it seems eventually the game difficulty will be increased, getting more power-up is desirable. But, I've played and know the game enough to know that this new system is not gonna work and also not practical because of the following reasons:
1. Each arc and each game modes have different covenant meta. For example, in arc 1 keyflare covenant is not needed, but in arc 2 it is mandatory. If we ever get arc 3 or another game mode with different rule, it is most likely that the meta will change and if the player has put a lot of resources into the wrong covenant, it will feel really bad. 
2. New covenants. We don't know if we'll ever get new covenants set in the future, but if ever get one, it will also creates the same problem as mentioned in point 1 above.
3. Different enemy requires different team comp, different team requires different covenants. Swapping covenants around is just the nature of the game, you can't really avoid it.
4. Flexible awakener. Some awakeners have flexible kit and can use many kinds of covenant. For example, Arachne might want to use Dream of Medicine, Rabbit, Photosynthesis, etc. For awakener like this, it just doesn't make sense to give them bonding covenants.
5. Team unique covenant conflict. You've already addressed this issue, but I personally think being able to override bonding covenant with preset covenant won't solve the actual issue. What's the point of having bonding covenant if in the end we have to change covenants depending on the mode and the enemy.

For now, I think it's better to postpone it and try to come up with a better system. If it's implemented like this, most likely this will be a seemingly good but actually useless feature.

Previous D-Tide iteration made more sense sense to me. Largely because it remained consistent with current D-Tide and its purpose. Now with Emergency Gnosis being available again we are trading integrity of the endgame for more shinies. It doesn't even take much effort to get the main rewards, and we shouldn't compromise gameplay for those who don't interact with teambuilding systems and game mechanics. I also understand that this argument is less favorable in this iteration due to silver in nightmare mode, which is why, along with disabling emergency gnosis usage (or keeping it only one per D-Tide), I'd suggest moving a portion of silver to hard mode, so that most people with reasonable effort would be able to get majority of rewards

Part 2

D-Effect Zone
I think for now keeping the silver reward after clearing Nightmare (or maybe lower it Hard) is what matter the most, so the current change is good.

Another  concern among most players is the future difficulty, but I don't think we can have a productive discussion about it here, as the topic involves too many layers of problems. You promised that the game won't be balanced around AA, and I think this is still true, but at the same time, you also don't disclose what awakeners, what's your keeper level, how many +12 WoD and what enemy you're facing during testing. It is understandable that you do this to prevent leaks. But at the same time, veteran players know that keeper level and WoD actually matters more than getting AA in this game. So although you're technically not lying, there are many hidden issues to this that cause anxiety to the players. That's why it's difficult to talk about difficulty without having to experience it first.

I suggest for now just do it and adjust the difficulty accordingly later. Also, instead of promising there won't be powercreep or difficulty increase (which I think unavoidable at this point), I think it's better to reassure and show the player that you'll constantly tweak the enemy that are problematic, buffing the weak awakeners, and maybe adding new system to increase the power level to keep up with the enemy HP and damage inflation.

gnosis change had 2 potential reasons/justifications: shrinking the power and skill gaps between beginners and veterans, and greed.

that aside, i like the idea of meta-progression where you can gather/craft consumable items to use for challenging content, most games that have them usually don't make a good use out of them, and they're usually forbidden in endgame, but in morimens i think it would fit in.
